source.name: Dylan Bachelet / The Great British Bake Off
source.author: Dylan Bachelet

meta.description: Enriched tangzhong rolls with Korean fermented chili paste and confit garlic. Paul Hollywood handshake recipe from GBBO Season 15 Bread Week.

change_log.summary: Swirl shape (cinnamon-roll style) becomes standard — roll-out, fill with butter + confit garlic, slice into 12. Replaces round ball shaping. Muffin tin replaces sheet pan. Scoring removed. Rolling difficulty tips added. Reheat updated for layered structure.
First bake feedback: tangzhong to round 100g/20g ratio, sheet pan with parchment, full bulb garlic confit, bench rest before shaping, clearer glaze steps
Expanded confit garlic food safety notes with make-ahead overnight workflow and botulism risk clarification
Initial recipe adapted from Dylan Bachelet's GBBO Season 15 Bread Week buns with science-informed adjustments from multi-agent research

states.title: Prep Confit Garlic
states.direction: Peel garlic cloves and place in a small oven-safe dish. Pour olive oil over cloves until fully submerged. Preheat oven to 250°F (120°C).
states.exit_condition: Garlic cloves fully submerged in oil, oven preheating

notes.text: Can be done up to 2 weeks ahead — store confit garlic submerged in oil in the fridge. Flavor improves over the first few days.

Food safety: refrigerate confit garlic within 2 hours. Never store at room temperature — garlic submerged in oil is anaerobic, exactly what C. botulinum needs. Fridge temps halt toxin production. Safe up to 7 days refrigerated (FDA guideline). Once garlic is removed from oil and chopped, the anaerobic seal is broken and botulism risk is over.
Make-ahead overnight: confit evening before, cool, refrigerate submerged in oil. Next morning pull garlic out, chop, fold into dough. Flavor actually improves overnight.

states.title: Bake Confit Garlic
states.direction: Bake garlic in oil at 250°F (120°C) for 2 hours until cloves are pale golden and completely soft.
states.exit_condition: Garlic cloves pale golden, knife slides through with zero resistance

notes.text: Stovetop alternative: lowest heat for 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Watch for garlic darkening past pale gold.

states.title: Chop Confit Garlic
states.direction: Remove garlic cloves from oil with a slotted spoon. Cool briefly, then rough chop into small pieces. Reserve the garlic-infused oil separately.
states.exit_condition: Garlic rough chopped, confit oil reserved in separate container

notes.text: The confit oil is liquid gold — use 1-2 tbsp in place of some dough butter for extra garlic depth, or save for cooking.

states.title: Make Tangzhong
states.direction: Combine water and bread flour in a small saucepan. Whisk until smooth with no lumps. Heat over medium-low, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens to a thick paste (about 2 minutes). Remove from heat and cool completely. Add all tangzhong to dough — do not discard any.
states.exit_condition: Thick, glossy paste that leaves trails when stirred. Cooled to room temperature.

notes.text: Tangzhong gelatinizes starch, trapping moisture for a softer crumb that stays fresh 3-4 days. This is the technique that gives these buns their signature pillowy texture.

states.title: Bloom Yeast
states.direction: Warm milk to 110°F (43°C). Stir in 4g sugar until dissolved, then sprinkle yeast over surface. Let sit until foamy, about 5 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Yeast mixture foamy and actively bubbling

states.title: Mix Dough
states.direction: Combine bread flour, remaining sugar, gochujang, and salt in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, stir egg and melted butter into the cooled tangzhong. Add the tangzhong mixture and yeast-milk mixture to the dry ingredients. Stir with a rubber spatula until a shaggy dough forms.
states.exit_condition: Shaggy dough formed, no dry flour visible. Dough will be sticky — this is expected.

notes.text: Gochujang adds hidden water (~44% moisture) and salt (~8%). The dough will feel wetter than typical enriched dough — don't add extra flour yet.

states.title: Knead Dough
states.direction: Transfer dough to a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky, about 8-10 minutes by hand. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with dough hook on medium-low for 6-8 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth and elastic, springs back when poked, no longer sticking to hands or counter

notes.text: If dough remains very sticky after 5 minutes of kneading, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time. The tangzhong and gochujang both add moisture.

states.title: First Rise
states.direction: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm spot until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
states.exit_condition: Dough has doubled in volume — poke test: finger indent fills back slowly

states.title: Fold in Confit Garlic
states.direction: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently press to deflate. Spread ~15g of the chopped confit garlic evenly over the surface. Reserve ~10g confit garlic for the filling layer. Fold dough over itself several times to distribute garlic throughout.
states.exit_condition: Garlic pieces visibly distributed throughout dough, no large unworked pockets. ~10g confit garlic reserved for filling.

notes.text: Don't over-knead — just fold enough to distribute. The garlic pieces should create pockets of flavor in the finished crumb.
Save remaining confit garlic beyond the 10g filling reserve — great on toast, stirred into rice, or mixed into compound butter.

states.title: Pre-Shape & Roll Rectangle
states.direction: Pat dough into a rough rectangle on a lightly floured surface. Cover with plastic wrap or a towel and rest 15-20 minutes for gluten relaxation. After resting, roll to a 40x30cm rectangle (~0.6-0.8cm thick). Roll from center outward, flipping and rotating every 3-4 passes with light pressure. If dough springs back more than 1cm during rolling, cover and rest another 10-15 minutes before continuing.
states.exit_condition: Even rectangle ~40x30cm, no dry spots or tears, uniform thickness

notes.text: 100% bread flour + gochujang's hidden salt tighten gluten significantly — staged bench rests are essential, not optional. Don't fight the dough.
Optional: chill dough 30-60 minutes in fridge before rolling for easier handling. Cold dough relaxes gluten and firms up butter.
Pre-shape by hand first, then refine with rolling pin. Center-outward strokes, light pressure. Flip and rotate every 3-4 passes to prevent sticking and ensure even thickness.

states.title: Fill & Roll
states.direction: Brush ~15g melted butter across the dough surface, leaving a 2.5cm border on the far long edge. Scatter ~10g minced confit garlic over the butter and press lightly to adhere. Starting from the near long edge, roll tightly into a cylinder, tucking under as you go. Pinch the seam firmly along the entire length. Rest seam-side-down for 2 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Firm, even cylinder ~30cm long, seam sealed and resting seam-side-down

notes.text: The bare border on the sealing edge is critical — butter on that strip prevents the seam from sealing and the roll unravels during proofing.

states.title: Portion & Pan
states.direction: Trim ~1cm off each end of the cylinder. Cut into 12 even pieces using geometric halving: cut in half, then each half into quarters, then each quarter into thirds. Use dental floss or a sharp serrated knife with gentle sawing motion — never press straight down or you'll compress the layers. Target ~67-68g per piece. Lightly grease muffin cups with butter or nonstick spray. Place each slice cut-side-up and press gently to contact the cup bottom.
states.exit_condition: 12 even portions in greased muffin cups, swirl pattern visible from top, each piece ~67-68g

notes.text: Geometric halving (half → quarters → thirds) gives more uniform pieces than measuring-and-cutting from one end.
Dental floss slides through enriched dough without compressing layers. Slide it under the cylinder, cross the ends over the top, and pull to cut cleanly.

states.title: Second Rise
states.direction: Cover muffin tin loosely with plastic wrap. Let buns rise in a warm spot until puffy and risen above the cup rims, about 45 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Buns puffy, risen above muffin cup rims, swirl layers visibly expanded

reminders.prompt: How do the buns look? Puffy and above the rims?

states.title: Egg Wash
states.direction: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly beat the remaining egg and brush over the tops of all buns, getting into the swirl crevices.
states.exit_condition: All buns evenly coated with egg wash, swirl tops glistening

notes.text: No scoring needed for swirl buns — the spiral pattern provides visual interest and natural expansion points during baking.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25-30 minutes, rotating pan halfway through, until buns are deep golden brown.
states.exit_condition: Deep golden brown on top, internal temperature reads 190°F (88°C)

notes.text: Gochujang's sugars accelerate browning — check at 20 minutes and tent with foil if the tops are getting too dark before the interior is done.

states.title: Cool in Pan
states.direction: Transfer pan to a wire rack. Let buns cool in the pan for 10 minutes before applying glaze or serving.
states.exit_condition: Buns cool enough to handle but still warm — ideal temperature for glaze absorption

states.title: Mix Honey-Soy Glaze
states.direction: Stir together honey and light soy sauce in a small bowl until combined. In a separate container, melt butter. Keep the honey-soy mixture and melted butter separate — they are applied in sequence.
states.exit_condition: Honey-soy mixture smooth and uniform, butter melted

notes.text: This glaze is optional but community-tested — Sophie Bamford's most popular upgrade to Dylan's original. Sweet-salty-umami without tipping into dessert territory.

states.title: Apply Glaze & Finish
states.direction: Brush honey-soy mixture over warm buns. Then brush melted butter on top. Sprinkle sesame seeds over all buns.
states.exit_condition: All buns coated with glaze, butter, and sesame seeds. Glossy finish visible.

notes.text: Order matters: honey-soy first (soaks in), then butter (seals and shines), then sesame seeds (stick to butter).
If making ahead: store unglazed. Reheat buns, then glaze while hot for best results.

methods.detail: Wrap in foil and heat at 300°F (150°C) for 8-10 minutes. Foil traps steam to keep the swirl layers moist. Unwrap last 2 minutes for a slightly crisp exterior.
Wrap loosely in foil, 300°F (150°C) for 3-4 minutes. Without foil the exposed layers dry out fast. Watch the gochujang sugars — they brown quickly.

Place damp paper towel over bun, microwave 15-20 seconds on high. Best for single servings — steam from the towel keeps the swirl layers soft. Don't overheat or the butter in the layers will make the bun greasy.

techniques.name: Tangzhong (Water Roux)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official recipe + all 4 copycat recreations
techniques.rationale: Pre-gelatinized starch doubles moisture retention, producing soft pillowy crumb that stays fresh 3-4 days

techniques.name: Gochujang in Dough
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official + 3/4 copycats mix into dough, not just filling
techniques.rationale: Distributes fermented chili flavor and color throughout. ~8% baker's percentage for balanced heat

techniques.name: Confit Garlic (folded after first rise)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official method — garlic folded in post-rise to preserve gluten
techniques.rationale: Mellow, sweet garlic that holds shape as pockets in the crumb. Post-rise fold avoids disrupting gluten network

techniques.name: Honey-Soy Post-Bake Glaze
techniques.rationale: Sweet-salty-umami finish. Butter layer prevents stickiness. Most popular non-original addition

cook_log.summary: First bake — taste was good but crumb was a bit dense. Needs more reps with enriched dough. Confit garlic came out tougher than expected. Lots of recipe step feedback captured for a future version bump.
notes: 5:33pm 4/16 — Started confit garlic in oven at 250°F for 2 hours, following a YouTube guide. Confit came out tougher than expected — unsure what target texture should be.
Made tangzhong at easier ratio: 100g water and 20g flour (yields extra). Referenced a YouTube tangzhong guide.
Mix-dough step felt overloaded — bouncing between different ingredients, mise en place wasn't helpful for this step's flow.
Forgot to start first rise timer.
Chopped confit garlic and folded into dough during first rise — timing made sense but could complicate batch cleaning.
Divided at ~79g per ball (recipe says 75g). Initially unsure about creating surface tension — let balls rest on mat, then shaped gloveless. Will improve with practice.
"Prepared pan" instruction was unclear — didn't know if it meant oiled, parchment, etc. Never figured it out.
11:24am — In oven at 350°F. Rotated at 15 min. Pulled at ~25 min — internal temp around 210°F (recipe exit condition says 190°F).
Applied honey-soy glaze, waited 5 min before butter application.
Crumb a bit dense but taste was good overall. Needs more reps with enriched dough. Wants confit chopped finer and more evenly distributed.
Want buns shaped more consistently — similar size and look across all 10. Probably needs more reps.

cook_log.summary: Second bake — 12 smaller buns (68g each) in cupcake pan. Better proofing via feel test, improved shaping. Pulled at 20 min but still hit 210°F. Confit super soft but want more — use all garlic next time. Accidental 40g honey was too sweet. Gochujang heat hitting back of throat.
notes: 6:14pm — Dough weight 782g pre-confit. Divided into 12 pieces targeting 68g each (5g variance). Cupcake pan experiment.
6:18pm — Confit totaled ~48g including absorbed oils (~1 full bulb). Dried oil off garlic before chopping.
6:52pm — Better proofing this time — did feel/poke test before shaping, dough had noticeable air inside.
6:55pm — Shaping noticeably improved over bake #1. Still too little confit — want to use all garlic next time.
Confit garlic was super soft this time (vs. tough in bake #1). Now thinking bake #1's firmer texture was more desirable — needs more research on target confit texture.
7:58pm — Accidental 40g honey in glaze. Too sweet — 30g is the right amount.
8:01pm — Considered misting tops with water to slow surface browning, didn't try.
8:08pm — Internal 210°F at 20 min at 350°F. Pulled at 20 min (5 min earlier than bake #1). Crust golden brown.
8:10pm — Didn't oil cupcake pan (predicted critical miss). Buns came out okay but will try oil next time.
8:43pm — Only need 4g sesame (recipe says 5g). Rested 30 min before glazing.
Gochujang possibly too much — spicy on back of throat. Considering reducing amount.
One bun bloomed/blistered rather than staying smooth — glaze absorbed deeper into the crumb. Prefers this. Thinking shallower format + more surface area = better glaze saturation.

cook_log.summary: Third bake — A/B test with 6 cinnamon-roll swirls vs 6 standard scored buns. Swirl style was the clear winner for bread flavor and glaze surface. Confit 43g from ~1.5 bulbs made 2 days prior. Swirl approach likely becomes v3 standard shape.
notes: 1:52pm — 76.5°F ambient, 56% humidity at mix.
2:14pm — Dough temp 75°F before bulk.
3:03pm — Prepped confit during initial proof. 43g after draining oil from confit made two days ago. Felt like almost 1.5 bulbs. More garlic is better for this recipe.
4:34pm — Split batch: 6 cinnamon-roll style swirls + 6 regular scored buns. Intentional A/B test. Varying swirl sizes helped determine target look — needs uniformity practice.
4:34pm — Short on butter but had enough for dough step. Made do with minimal butter wash.
4:35pm — Rotated oven at ~12 min mark. 350°F. Preheated while shaping.
4:35pm — Sprayed tops with water to prevent scorching.
4:36pm — For swirl style: added melted butter pat and minced garlic before rolling up. Theory is butter/garlic gelatinizes at bottom of roll.
4:50pm — Out after 24 min total. Pulled at 20, thought tops could be browner, added 4 more minutes. Internal ~210°F. Center rolls weren't browning evenly — uniformity issue.
5:34pm — Swirl style is a winner. Better overall bread flavor than standard round buns.
7:49pm — Swirly variation with melted butter should become standard v3. Consider putting butter/confit directly in the roll-up for more even distribution across all rolls.
7:50pm — Need to figure out uniform roll sizing for swirl approach. If making 12, even sizes = even cooking.
